newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while pork belly futures calls ranged from 0.200 cent lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.

Mostly steady to weak cash hog indications as rain in the Midwest allowed increased hog movement will likely put pressure on hog futures. Deferred months may see added pressure from the expected bearish Hogs and Pigs report this Friday and technically weak market, they said.
Bull spreading may again provide support to the nearby, they added.

Analyst estimates on Friday's quarterly report put June 1 all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms at an average 102.9 percent of a year ago and ranged from 101.7 to 105 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 104.3 percent in a range of 103 to 106 percent and hogs kept for market averaged 102.6 percent of a year ago in a range of 101 to 105 pct.
Pork belly futures calls ranged mixed after the choppy action of recent sessions. Trade could again be uneven as the market awaits Friday's hog report, they said.

Tuesday's weekly CME out-of-town storage report provided little direction as movement into storage was in line with expectations. However, reports of product moving out of storage this week may prompt fresh buying interest in futures, they said.
CME reported a net in-movement of 205,000 lbs last week which compared with earlier analyst expectations of unchanged to in 200,000 lbs.
